steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The oikos (household) was the basic social unit: the male head (kyrios) controlled the family, property and dependants

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Athenian women lived largely secluded lives in the women's quarters (gynaikeion); they could not vote, own property or conduct business independently

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The symposium was an elite male drinking party featuring conversation, music and entertainment; it was central to aristocratic social and political networking

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Slavery was fundamental to the Athenian economy: slaves worked in homes, workshops, mines and fields; they had no legal rights

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What was the oikos and how was it organised? | Q: What restrictions did Athenian women face? | Q: What happened at a symposium?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: The oikos was the household unit controlled by the kyrios (male head). It included his wife, children, slaves and all property. The kyrios had legal authority over all members. Women managed the house | Citizen women could not vote, hold office, or own property. They needed a male kyrios (father, husband or guardian) to represent them legally. They lived largely secluded in the gynaikeion, rarely lef | Elite men reclined on couches in the andron (men's room), drank diluted wine, were entertained by musicians, dancers and hetairai, and engaged in conversation covering politics, philosophy and poetry.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Oikos = basic unit, kyrios = male head Women: secluded, no vote, no property, kyrios represents them Symposium = elite male networking, NOT just a party Slavery = fundamental to Athenian economy and citizen leisure
